commands.check: Check what the page loads before consent

cookie.after_reject: After "Reject all" the cookie {name} ({domain}) is newly set and kept {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
cookie.after_reject_session: After "Reject all" the cookie {name} ({domain}) is newly set for the browser session.
cookie.before_consent: The cookie {name} ({domain}) is set before any consent and kept {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
cookie.before_consent_session: The cookie {name} ({domain}) is set before any consent, for the browser session.

request.after_reject: After "Reject all" the page still reaches {host} ({kind}, {count, plural, one {# request} other {# requests}}).
request.before_consent: Before any consent the page reaches {host} ({kind}, {count, plural, one {# request} other {# requests}}).

consent-check.name: Consent check
consent-check.notice: Technical pre-check, no legal advice: it shows what the page loads and stores before a choice and after "Reject all", not whether that is lawful.

caveat.cookiesUnread: The view's cookies could not be read.
caveat.firstPartyCookies: Only the cookies sent to the page's own address are read; cookies of other sites are not.
caveat.noRejectStep: "Reject all" is clicked only in a session of the check's own, so this run has no step after it.
caveat.notRejected: No "Reject all" button was found, so there is no step after it.
caveat.sessionKept: The check's session was not reported deleted.
caveat.viewSession: This run reads the view in its own session: a consent given earlier there hides findings.

panel.empty: Check the page to see which other sites it reaches and which cookies it sets before any consent.
panel.export: Write the result to the out folder
panel.firstParty: {count, plural, one {# request} other {# requests}} to the page's own site

mode.session: A fresh session of the check's own, deleted afterwards.
mode.view: The view as it is, read only.

panel.noFindings: No findings: nothing reaches another site and no cookie is set before consent.
panel.reported: {count, plural, one {# finding} other {# findings}} sent to the findings panel.

cookie.after_reject: A cookie that is not essential is set after "Reject all"
cookie.before_consent: A cookie that is not essential is set before consent

request.after_reject: Another site is reached after "Reject all"
request.before_consent: Another site is reached before consent

allowHosts.description: Hosts counted as the page's own, such as your CDN: no finding. A host such as cdn.example.com, or *.example.com for a domain and its subdomains.
allowHosts.help: Requests to these hosts count as the page's own and make no finding; they are still listed. Example: cdn.example.com, *.example-cdn.net for a domain and its subdomains.
allowHosts.label: Hosts of your own

essentialCookies.description: Cookies of your own that are strictly necessary: no finding. A name such as cart_id, or a prefix such as pref_*.
essentialCookies.help: Session, CSRF and consent manager cookies are known already. Name your own strictly necessary cookies here; they are listed as essential and make no finding. Example: cart_id, pref_* for every cookie starting with pref_.
essentialCookies.label: Essential cookies

rejectStep.description: After the first capture, click the banner's "Reject all" in the check's own session and capture again.
rejectStep.help: On, the check clicks the "Reject all" button of a known consent banner in its own session and records what the page still loads and sets; the differences are shown. Off, it records the page before consent only.
rejectStep.label: Check after "Reject all"

tools.check: Loads `url` or the page of the target view in a fresh session of its own, without consent, and lists the requests to other sites (host and kind: script, pixel, font, iframe), the cookies (name, domain, lifetime; never a value) and the localStorage keys; with the reject step on, clicks "Reject all" and lists them once more, with the differences and the findings. The session is deleted afterwards. `export` also writes the result to the out folder. A technical pre-check, no legal advice.
